labels.text: Search sessions by title or message text

S34.02.needs: a past conversation with a known word in its title or messages
S34.02.note: The sidebar also has a "Search sessions" box that appears above the session list, but the code shows it only when the session list has rows.
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P and type "Code: Show Sessions History". Press Enter.
In the box that opens, read the placeholder "Search sessions by title or message text".
Type a word from the title or from a message of a past chat that you know exists.
Wait a moment for the list to update, then check that the matching chat is listed and that unrelated chats are not.
Click or press Enter on the matching row to open it, and check that the chat opens.
S34.02.where: Command Palette > "Code: Show Sessions History", then type in the box titled "Sessions history"

S34.03.needs: an account with at least one project
S34.03.note: The code uses the generic quick pick, which matches typed text against the name, description and detail. The code does not show that a project's description is put in those fields, so a match by description is unverified.
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P and type "Code: Show Projects". Press Enter.
Read the placeholder "Open a project…" in the box that opens.
Type a project name you created on the web.
Check that the matching project is listed.
Press Enter on the match and check that the project opens.
S34.03.where: Command Palette > "Code: Show Projects", then type in the box that says "Open a project…"

S34.05.needs: an account with at least one artifact
S34.05.note: The code uses the generic quick pick, which matches typed text against the name, description and detail. The code does not show that artifact content (not just the title) is searched, so a match on content is unverified.
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P and type "Code: Show Artifacts". Press Enter.
Read the placeholder "Open an artifact…" in the box that opens.
Type a word from an artifact's title.
Check that the matching artifact is listed and unrelated ones are not.
Press Enter on the match and check that the artifact opens.
S34.05.where: Command Palette > "Code: Show Artifacts", then type in the box that says "Open an artifact…"

S34.06.needs: a work source connected to the account, such as Drive, Slack or Notion
S34.06.note: The search happens on the server when a chat request is made (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts). The extension has a start-screen group named "Connected apps" with an "Ask with it" action (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/webviewContent.ts), but I found no control in the extension to connect Drive, Slack or Notion. I searched for "connector", "knowledge" and "collection" in apps/extension-vscode/src.

S34.07.needs: a search key if the account is in Local or BYOK mode ("Set up web search" in the same menu)
S34.07.note: The menu text says "Local privacy mode refuses network", so web search is refused in that mode. I did not check the server rules for when a search key is needed.
steps: Open the chat sidebar and click the "+" button under "Attach or use tools".
Click "Browse the web" so it is checked.
Check that the strip "Browse the web for current sources" appears above the input.
Type a question that needs current information, such as today's news on a topic, and send it.
Check that the answer uses web results and that sources are listed under the answer.
S34.07.where: Sidebar chat > "+" button (title "Attach or use tools") > "Browse the web"

S34.19.needs: a project with knowledge files, if testing project knowledge
S34.19.note: I found no control in apps/extension-vscode to put chosen sources into a named collection or to limit a chat's search to one. The only related screen is the read-only "Knowledge files" list in a project (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/projects/projectActions.ts), whose description reads "Knowledge files are added and removed there", meaning on the web. I searched for "collection", "knowledge" and "source" in apps/extension-vscode/src.

S34.27.needs: a web-sourced answer with at least one source ("Browse the web" turned on)
S34.27.note: The code accepts only http and https addresses for these links, and I did not find the code that opens the link itself.
steps: Ask a question that gets a web-sourced answer, using "Browse the web" if needed.
Under the answer, find the disclosure labelled "{count} sources" and click it to open the list.
Hover a source link to check its full address.
Click the source link and check that the original page opens in the browser.
S34.27.where: Sidebar chat > an answer's "{count} sources" disclosure > click a source link
